title: Underwater research on neutrinos is starting in Lake Superior
excerpt: An underwater neutrino research project is going to be underway shortly, with sensors going into Lake Superior.
content:
The R/V Neil Armstrong has made her first voyage to the Twin Ports. She’s normally stationed out of Massachusetts, and has sailed all over the world. But now, it’s a new horizon here.

Her task is to help place neutrino sensors into the water of Lake Superior near Two Harbors.

Neutrinos are one of the fundamental particles of the universe, but the one scientists know the least about. There’s a billion of them for every proton or electron.

A lab in Chicago has been beaming neutrinos to Ash River or Soudan since 2005. Now, the goal is to study how they interact in the water.

“This is our chance to see the ones that have been going through Lake Superior all along and see what we can learn from them,” Alec Habig explained. He’s a Professor of Physics at UMD.

The sensors will look for a light that is a result of neutrino activity. It will feed the data through cables that are connected to a data collection system on shore. This is only temporary, as the beam is set to stop in February.

There are five sensor arrays that will be taken out, one at a time, to the deployment space. The plan is to get one out there this week yet.

Rob Munier is the VP of Marine Facilities and Operations of Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution. WHOI for short, and that group runs the Neil Armstrong.

“So our job here is we’ve engineered these structures behind you to host the detectors. We’ve developed a solution to install the cables on shore.We are providing the Neil Armstrong, which is a very sophisticated vessel that allows us to do this in a very precise and safe way. Normally we do this in the ocean, but we are doing it here because we can bring those skills to a different environment, but one that has a lot of the same types of challenges,” Munier explained.

There are around 22 people who crew on the Neil Armstrong, and then scientists will also come on board for the installation.

In the spring, another vessel will retrieve the sensors. But the cables will remain to collect data about the lake.

DARPA funding is helping with the project. They are a division of the Department of Defense. Program manager John Bruzzese said, “We don’t know what the future is. It’s DARPA’s role to continue monitoring, funding research so that when we understand, we can prepare our nation for that new world.”

There is also neutrino research underway on Lake Vermilion.
